**Review: peppermint product page copy**

Claims list:

| Claim | Status |
|---|---|
| "Just peppermint leaves, nothing else" | Product fact (ingredients), fine as written |
| "Cool and clean after a big meal" | Flavour/sensory description, fine |
| "a natural detox" | Unsupported. Health claim; "detox" is not on the allowlist and is not a permitted product fact. |
| "aids weight loss" | Unsupported. Health claim, and one that ad platforms and UK regulators (ASA/CAP, and the UK Nutrition and Health Claims rules) treat strictly. No source or authorisation. |
| "Certified organic by the Soil Association" | Allowlisted |

**Problems**

1. "a natural detox": an unauthorised health claim. Herbal teas can't be marketed as detoxifying under UK/GB health claims rules, and nothing in the brand policy backs it up.
2. "aids weight loss": an unauthorised, regulated health claim. It must be removed. It also can't be softened to "can help"; there is no source to support even the softer version.

**Suggested compliant version**

> Peppermint. Just peppermint leaves, nothing else. Cool and clean after a big meal. Certified organic by the Soil Association.

Slop and structure check: no ban-list words, no exclamation marks, no rhetorical opener. The opening is fine as a short product-name lead, though it could carry a fact sooner (for example, naming the sizes or origin if you have them).

The draft should not be published as written.

```json
{"issues": [{"quote": "a natural detox", "type": "health_claim"}, {"quote": "aids weight loss", "type": "health_claim"}], "publish": false}
```
